content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes a method for 3D hand mesh reconstruction based on 2D feature extractor (with hourglass model), followed by decoder that maps the 2D features into 3D mesh. The main modification compared to previous models is in the mesh decoder, where the generated 3D mesh vertices are projected to the 2D image plane to retrieve pixel-aligned features, then upscaled to the next mesh scale level.  With this, the aggregation of pixel-aligned features at different scales is reinforced for creating the 3D mesh. Evaluations of the proposed model on the FreiHand dataset show comparable results to SOTA.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

(*) The paper is clearly written and deals with an interesting problem.

(*) The 3D supervision and 2D auxiliary supervision seem to be useful for the training procedure 

Weaknesses:

(*) Technical novelty is somewhat limited. I am not sure how much the pixel aligned mapping contributes to performance, since some alignment and pyramid scale are already implicitly implemented in previous models.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The submission proposed a framework that can achieve a single-image reconstruction of the hand. They design a 2D network to extract the features and aggregate the 2D features and 3D geometrical features from the mesh encoder in a coarse to fine manner. In the meanwhile, the 3D-to-2D projection is conducted by combining the 3D vertex convolution and self-attention. All the 2D feature extractor and 3D mesh extractor is in a coarse-to-fine manner, which can leverage the multi-scale information. The experimental results demonstrate better performance in more challenging cases.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1.The paper is well-written.
2.The statement of the contribution is clear, but not significant.
3.The pipeline and diagram are very clear, which makes the readers easier to follow the work.
Weakness:
1.The technical novelty is not new. After reading the paper, the technical points are similar to pixel2mesh, which also uses the 2D and 3D feature network to extract the features and project the mesh vertex to the 2D image in a multi-scale manner. Is there any difference? Or only the submission simply apply the pixel2mesh on the hand dataset. There must be a more comprehensive discussion.
2.The experiments are insufficient. For the unclear table 4(mentioned above), there are not any visualization results that incorporate with the table, ie. the visualization comparison with the other baselines in table 4.
3.For the organization of the experiment, the comparison with other baselines (including the qualitative and quantitative evaluations) should be exchanged in the place of ablations. A suggestion: the ablation studies should show some visualization cases that will be more helpful to demonstrate the superiority of the proposed methods.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
> In Table 4, what does the bold font mean? For each metric, the best one is marked wrongly. The authors should check it carefully for a clear statement. And, the authors claim that ‘All of our approaches achieve state-of-the-art for all the metrics.’ in Sec 4.3. It is not convincing.
> In sec 3.3, why the coarse-to-fine mesh topologies are acquired by mesh simplification, not the subdivision? Is it a typo, or an inverse process?
> How to conduct the projection from 3D to 2D. If the process is not accurate, will the performance of the proposed method be influenced?
> If there are multiple hands in a single image, could the method also work well?
> The submission lacks detailed architecture and implementation, and reproducibility is not easy for the beginner of deep learning. If the research is familiar to the field of image-based reconstruction, I think the reproducibility is not very heavy work. It is best if the author could release the code.
> For the non-parametric design, the first mesh decoder M_4, how to ensure the connection of the vertices is reasonable. The visualization comparison with the parametric methods is very essential. And for the necessity of the non-parametric design for the hand prediction, I think the parametric-based methods are enough since the hand motion is relatively simple. Why use the non-parametric design?
content.summary_of_the_review: According to the above concerns and issues, I think the paper has limited technical contribution and the motivation is not clear for the non-parametric designs. Especially, the experiment is not sufficient for the visualization results. So, this submission is still a certain distance from the bar  of this conference, I am negative for the submission.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a non-parametric method for hand mesh reconstruction. The proposed method first extracts multi-scale image features and then projects the vertex position of multi-resolution hand meshes to retrieve pixel-aligned features for the update of the hand meshes. Graph convolution and self-attention are also leveraged to improve feature learning. Comprehensive ablation studies are included to validate the design of the proposed method. State-of-the-art results are achieved on the FreiHAND dataset.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
This paper is overall well-written with clear motivation and strong experimental results. Using the multi-scale and pixel-aligned features makes sense and is technically sound. The results on the FreiHAND dataset are strong. 

My main concerns about this paper are the novelty of the proposed method as it seems to be a combination of two existing well-known approaches PyMAF and Graphormer. 

Moreover, the proposed method is only evaluated on FreiHAND. It is not clear about the generalization of the proposed method on other datasets. There are no video results to demonstrate its superior performance to other methods on real-world scenes.

From the failure cases in Fig. 4, the proposed method seems to be not very robust to occlusions. Though most existing methods may fail under these challenging cases.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The presentation of this paper is clear. The experiments can be easily reproduced as this paper includes enough technical details. The novelty of this work is limited as the proposed method seems to be a combination of existing approaches.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper presents a non-parametric approach for hand mesh reconstruction by using multi-scale pixel-aligned features. The results of the proposed method are strong and outperform existing approaches. My main concern is about its novelty. I would recommend further extending the proposed method with additional technical contributions and submitting it to another venue.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper proposes a non-parametric mesh reconstruction method leveraging the pixel-aligned feature for hand mesh reconstruction from monocular RGB images. It contains a multi-scale 2D feature extractor, a pixel-aligned feature mapping module, and a multi-scale 3D mesh decoder. The main contribution is the pixel-aligned feature mapping module, which can extract the per-vertex feature from the 2D feature map. This method achieves comparable results on the 3D mesh reconstruction dataset FreiHand.
However, using the pixel-aligned feature for mesh reconstruction has already been used in previous methods of other tasks（\eg, pifu, pifuhd). The novelty and contribution of this work are limited.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength and Weakness:
Strength: 
This method achieves a comparable SOTA result on the FreiHand dataset.
The ablation study of the mapping module shows that exploiting pixel-aligned features can improve hand reconstruction performance.

Weakness:
- The results only illustrate the effectiveness of this work on one typical dataset. This method seems can be applied for 3D human body reconstruction. More results on other 3D hands (or body) mesh reconstruction datasets should be included.
- The qualitative results should include the results of other SOTA methods to make the effectiveness of this work more convincing.

Clarity:
In Eq.4, the meaning of "MHSA" is not given. 
typo: 
In the introduction section, 
"Their pipelines (Kulon et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2021b; Lin et al., 2021b) usually consist of three stages: ... "
content.summary_of_the_review: Technical side, the novelty is incremental as the modules in this work are already been used in many other previous works. Moreover, the performance improvement on the typical hand reconstruction dataset is marginal.

content.title: Pixel-Aligned Non-parametric Hand Mesh Reconstruction
content.abstract: Non-parametric mesh reconstruction has recently shown significant progress in 3D hand and body applications. In these methods, mesh vertices and edges are visible to neural networks, enabling the possibility to establish a direct mapping between 2D image pixels and 3D mesh vertices. In this paper, we seek to establish and exploit this mapping with a simple and compact architecture. The network is designed with these considerations: 1) aggregating both local 2D image features from the encoder and 3D geometric features captured in the mesh decoder; 2) decoding coarse-to-fine meshes along the decoding layers to make the best use of the hierarchical multi-scale information.  Specifically, we propose an end-to-end pipeline for hand mesh recovery tasks which consists of three phases: a 2D feature extractor constructing multi-scale feature maps, a feature mapping module transforming local 2D image features to 3D vertex features via 3D-to-2D projection, and a mesh decoder combining the graph convolution and self-attention to reconstruct mesh. The decoder aggregate both local image features in pixels and geometric features in vertices. It also regresses the mesh vertices in a coarse-to-fine manner, which can leverage multi-scale information. By exploiting the local connection and designing the mesh decoder, Our approach achieves state-of-the-art for hand mesh reconstruction on the public FreiHAND dataset.
